blocks.task_summary: Find the Maclaurin series for f(x) = e^x sin x up to and including the x^3 term.
method_path: Recognize standard Maclaurin series: e^x = 1 + x + x^2/2! + x^3/3! + ... and sin x = x - x^3/3! + ...
Multiply the two series, retaining terms up to x^3
State result: f(x) = x + x^2 + x^3/3 + ...
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2 (derivatives): Compute f prime, f double prime, f triple prime using product rule; evaluate at x=0; substitute into Maclaurin formula to obtain f(x) = x + x^2 + x^3/3 + ...

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: recognition of both known series (M1); attempt to multiply the two series up to x^3 (M1); intermediate expression (A1); final series x + x^2 + x^3/3 + ... (A1). METHOD 2: f'(x) = e^x cos x + e^x sin x (A1); f''(x)=2e^x cos x, f'''(x)=2e^x(cos x - sin x) (A1); substitute x=0 (M1); obtain series (A1).

blocks.task_summary: Hence find an approximate value for the definite integral from 0 to 1/2 of e^(x^2) sin(x^2) dx.
method_path: Substitute x -> x^2 into series: e^(x^2) sin(x^2) = x^2 + x^6/3 + ...
Integrate termwise from 0 to 1/2: integral x^2 dx = x^3/3, integral x^6/3 dx = x^7/21
Evaluate at limits: [x^3/3 + x^5/5 + x^7/21] from 0 to 1/2

evidence.basis: e^(x^2) sin(x^2) = x^2 + x^6/3 + ... (A1); substitute and attempt to integrate (M1); obtain [x^3/3 + x^5/5 + x^7/21] (A1); final 61/105 (A1).

blocks.task_summary: (i) Show g''(x) = 2(g'(x) - g(x)) for g(x)=e^x cos x. (ii) Hence deduce g^(4)(x) = 2(g'''(x) - g''(x)).
method_path: (i) Apply product rule: g'(x) = e^x cos x - e^x sin x
Compute 2(g'(x) - g(x)) = -2e^x sin x, confirming identity
accepted_alternatives: Accept working with each side separately to obtain -2e^x sin x for both parts.

evidence.basis: (i) attempt product rule (M1); g'(x) = e^x cos x - e^x sin x (A1); g''(x) = -2e^x sin x (A1); show g''(x) = 2(g'(x)-g(x)) (A1). (ii) g'''(x) = 2(g''(x)-g'(x)) (A1); g^(4)(x) = 2(g'''(x)-g''(x)) AG. Note: Accept working with each side separately.

blocks.task_summary: Using the result from part (c), find the Maclaurin series for g(x) = e^x cos x up to and including the x^4 term.

evidence.basis: attempt to substitute x=0 into a derivative (M1); g(0)=1, g'(0)=1, g''(0)=0 (A1); g'''(0)=-2, g^(4)(0)=-4 (A1); attempt to substitute into Maclaurin formula (M1); g(x)=1+x-x^3/3-x^4/6+... (A1). Do not award marks for approaches not using part (c).

blocks.task_summary: Hence, or otherwise, determine lim_{x->0} (e^x cos x - 1 - x) / x^3.
method_path: Substitute Maclaurin series for e^x cos x: numerator = (1+x-x^3/3-x^4/6+...)-1-x = -x^3/3-x^4/6+...
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2 (l'Hopital): 0/0 form; apply l'Hopital three times: lim g'(x)/(3x^2) = lim g''(x)/(6x) = lim g'''(x)/6 = -2/6 = -1/3.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: substitute series (M1); obtain lim [-1/3 - x/6 + ...] (A1); answer -1/3 (A1). METHOD 2: indeterminate 0/0, apply l'Hopital (M1); successive applications yield lim (-2e^x sin x - 2e^x cos x)/6 (A1); answer -1/3 (A1).
